issues.legal_issue: A substitute arbitrator may be appointed when a named arbitrator’s mandate terminates in a court-referred arbitration, unless the parties’ agreement expressly or by necessary implication bars substitution.
material_facts: While a suit was pending, the parties agreed in consent terms to refer unresolved disputes to a named retired judge for arbitration.
The court recorded the consent terms, disposed of the suit, and referred the unresolved disputes to the named arbitrator.
The arbitrator resigned, and the agreement contained no express or implied prohibition on appointing a substitute or indication that only the named arbitrator could decide the disputes.
The party seeking a replacement applied to the same High Court that had recorded the consent terms and appointed the original arbitrator; that court appointed a substitute arbitrator.
issues.conclusion: The High Court correctly appointed a substitute arbitrator. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 15(1) and (2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, when an arbitrator’s mandate terminates, a substitute is to be appointed according to the rules applicable to the original appointment; those rules include the parties’ arbitration agreement. Read liberally and purposively to promote effective arbitration, Section 15(2) permits substitution unless the agreement expressly or by necessary implication prohibits it. Sections 15(3) and (4), concerning continuation of proceedings and preservation of prior rulings after replacement, support that construction. Section 89 CPC provides for court referral to arbitration by agreement in a pending suit; a consent order is more than a contract because it carries the command of a judge. The Court relied on Yashwith Constructions (P) Ltd. v. Simplex Concrete Piles India Ltd., SBP and Company v. Patel Engineering Ltd., ACC Ltd. v. Global Cements Ltd., Parbhat General Agencies v. Union of India, C.F. Angadi v. Y.S. Hirannayya, and P. Anand Gajapati Raju v. P.V.G. Raju.

rule.if: court_referred_arbitration and arbitrator_mandate_terminated and agreement_does_not_bar_substitution and original_appointment_made_by_court and substitute_sought_from_original_court

predicates.court_referred_arbitration: A court handling a suit referred unresolved disputes to arbitration after the parties agreed to that method of resolution.
predicates.arbitrator_mandate_terminated: The arbitrator appointed to decide the referred disputes withdrew, died, or otherwise ceased to hold the mandate.
predicates.agreement_does_not_bar_substitution: The parties’ agreement does not expressly or by necessary implication prohibit a substitute or make the original arbitrator uniquely indispensable.
predicates.original_appointment_made_by_court: The court made or adopted the appointment of the original arbitrator when recording the parties’ agreement.
predicates.substitute_sought_from_original_court: A party asked the court responsible for the original appointment to appoint a replacement.
predicates.original_court_may_appoint_substitute_ar: The court responsible for the original appointment may appoint a substitute arbitrator.

issues.definition: When a court referred agreed disputes to arbitration, the arbitrator’s mandate ended, the agreement did not bar replacement, and the original appointing court was asked to act, that court may appoint a substitute arbitrator.
